title: "Async Video vs Live Meetings: When a Video Saves Everyone Time" (blog explainer)

brief.motion: Brisk, confident pacing with soft ease-out arrivals and short overshoots on key words; the camera drifts slowly and makes one decisive push or pull per scene.
brief.story: We open in a dark, crowded calendar and move into light as the video earns its place. Dark scenes for the problem and the meeting, paper-bright scenes for the async solution, ending on a warm, open call to action.

scenes.narration: A lot of meetings are really presentations with a calendar invite. Here's when a video saves everyone time, and when to keep the meeting.
scenes.storyboard: Night stage: a tight grid of calendar blocks fills the frame and the camera slowly pushes in. On 'presentations with a calendar invite' one block flips to show a tiny slide icon, then the others flip in a ripple. On 'a video saves everyone time' the blocks dissolve away, leaving a single coral play button. The headline 'Async video vs live meetings' sets in at 120px with the subtitle beneath in mist. The original's overlapping title text is rebuilt cleanly; nothing else kept.

scenes.narration: If the content is mostly one-way, a video often wins. It reaches the manager, finance and IT, and lands in their morning, whether that's Perth or London.
scenes.storyboard: Paper stage, wide. On 'one-way' a single coral arrow shoots from a play button on the left. On 'the manager, finance and IT' it splits into three branches, each ending in a labelled avatar. On 'lands in their morning' each avatar gets a small rising sun. On 'Perth or London' the camera pulls back to reveal two clocks labelled Perth and London showing different times, both with sunrise. Headline 'Send a video when it's one-way' at top; the four bullets are cut and carried by the visual.

slide.title: Send a video when content is one-way
slide.text: Same information for everyone. Several people, at different times. Time zones get in the way. People need to think first

scenes.narration: But keep the meeting for real conversation. A good rule: if it's mostly you talking, send a video. If it's mostly them talking, meet.
scenes.storyboard: Night stage, close. Two speech bubbles face each other in teal and sky, pulsing back and forth on 'real conversation'. On 'mostly you talking' a single bubble swells huge on the left and morphs into a coral play button labelled 'Send a video'. On 'mostly them talking' the right side fills with many small bubbles that gather into a table icon labelled 'Meet'. The split-screen holds as a two-column rule. The four bullets are cut; the rule from the notes becomes the hero.

scenes.narration: A video only saves time if people watch it. Keep it short, tell them why it matters up front, and end with one clear next step.
scenes.storyboard: Paper stage. A horizontal video timeline bar draws across the frame on 'if people watch it'. On 'keep it short' the bar snaps shorter with a spring. On 'why it matters up front' a coral flag pops onto the start of the bar. On 'one clear next step' a teal arrow lands at the end of the bar labelled 'Next step'. Camera glides gently along the bar left to right. Headline 'Make a video people watch' at top-left; bullets cut.

slide.title: Make an async video people watch
slide.text: Keep it short, one topic. Say why it matters on slide one. Use headlines that make a point. End with one clear next step

scenes.narration: Instead of waiting a week for a follow-up meeting, send a five-minute narrated deck the next morning. The next meeting becomes questions, not a presentation.
scenes.storyboard: Ink stage, wide. A week-long calendar strip shows a grey meeting block far off on the right; on 'waiting a week' it greys out with a strike. On 'five-minute narrated deck' a coral video card titled 'Three changes that would halve your month-end reporting time' drops onto tomorrow morning, with a '5 min' tag. It forwards along lines to 'finance' and 'IT' chips. On 'questions, not a presentation' the next meeting block shrinks and fills with question marks. Hold on the shorter block.
